subject: Renewal + capacity uplift: pricing path and credit structure
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@herasys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + capacity uplift: pricing path and credit structure

Hi Asha —

Quick note ahead of our renewal later this quarter (term ends 2027-07-31). Congrats on the product launch roadmap — appreciate the heads-up that Hera expects a step up in inference volume (roughly 2–3x for Q3). To make sure we keep costs predictable while supporting the spike, we sketched two practical paths and attached a short draft SOW + your Q1 usage.

Option A — 12-month renewal + price hold + bridging credit (recommended for short runway):
- Baseline commit: 1,000,000 tokens/month (current baseline) at a 12-month term.
- Price hold: 20% hold on current per-token list rate for the baseline volume for the term.
- Bridging credit: $75,000 one-time credit applied to overage in the first billing quarter to smooth the pilot.

Option B — 24-month tiered commit (recommended if you want long-term unit economics):
- Tiered pricing: incremental discounts that trigger at 2M and 5M tokens/month, stepping down unit price by 10–18%.
- Lower upfront credit but deeper unit-price discounts after thresholds are reached.

For both options we can include a short-rate guarantee for the pilot period, and an SLO for median latency under your expected load. See attached 'usage_report_q1.csv' and the draft 'Hera_SOW_v3.pdf' for the exact numbers we used.

Can you share an updated monthly usage projection for July–Sept (even a simple estimate is fine)? I can sync our pricing model and put a formal side-by-side for you and procurement. If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the math.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Asha Patel <asha@herasys.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Gomez <rafael.gomez@herasys.com>, procurement@herasys.com
Date: 2027-06-11T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift: pricing path and credit structure

Thanks, Logan — this is helpful.

A few clarifying items from our side:
- We will very likely double capacity in July and approach ~2.5x by August depending on pilot results.
- Procurement (cc'd) will need a clear mapping of: committed baseline vs. overage treatment, how the bridging credit is applied (billing vs. credit note), and whether the price hold applies to committed + burst usage or only committed baseline.
- Rafael (CFO) wants a short-term rate guarantee for the 90-day pilot; can you confirm a hold window?

Please loop in your pricing/legal folks and share a short redlineable amendment. Procurement, can you confirm the internal timeline for approvals?

Best,
Asha
Asha Patel | Head of Platform, Hera Systems
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@herasys.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal + capacity uplift: pricing path and credit structure

Hi Asha — adding some specificity so procurement has numbers to work with. Quicknotes below; full math attached in the SOW draft.

Summary (Option A — 12m + bridging credit):
- Baseline commit: 1,000,000 tokens/month at current list $0.00080/token (pre-discount).
- Effective baseline price with 20% hold: $0.00064/token.
- Bridging credit: $75,000 applied as billing credit to Q3 invoices; it offsets overage charges first, then recurring overages while credit remains.
- Pilot rate guarantee: 90-day guarantee at the effective baseline price for committed volume + a 10% reserved burst allowance (i.e., we will not bill above the guaranteed price for the first 90 days for up to 1.1x baseline).

Alternative (Option B — 24m tiered):
- Commitment bands: 1–2M tokens/month (no change), 2–5M (-10% unit price after hitting 2M sustained for 60 days), >5M (-18% after 60 days).
- Lower one-time credit ($30k) but deeper long-term savings if you scale.

Operational notes:
- SLA & throughput: median inference tail latency SLO (p95 under expected concurrency) will be written into the amendment; we can agree on runbook and escalation paths.
- Billing mechanics: bridging credit will appear as a line item credit; overage calculations remain the same but are applied after credit exhaustion.
- Legal: attached 'Hera_SOW_v3.pdf' contains the amendment language.

If this looks okay, Logan and I will draft a short amendment + DocuSign package. Timeline-wise, signing by 2027-06-25 would let us put the rate hold into effect for a 2027-07-01 pilot start.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call with procurement this afternoon if that helps.
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Hera_SOW_v3.pdf, usage_report_q1.csv)
From: Asha Patel <asha@herasys.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@herasys.com, Rafael Gomez <rafael.gomez@herasys.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift: pricing path and credit structure

On Sat, Jun 12, Vanessa Ortiz wrote:
> If this looks okay, Logan and I will draft a short amendment + DocuSign package.

Thank you — that allays most concerns. Procurement: we'll review the amendment this week; main asks from our side:
- Confirm the 90-day pilot rate guarantee language (include explicit burst allowance cap).
- Add a short SLA clause that calls out target median latency and an escalation owner at Redwood for the pilot.
- Confirm how the $75k credit reduces our first-quarter invoices (credit note vs. refund).

If those items are ironed out, we can move forward with the 12-month path and the bridging credit. Can Logan/Vannesa send a redlineable amendment and the DocuSign link by EOD Tuesday (6/16)? Procurement aims to circulate internally by 6/18.

Regards,
Asha
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@herasys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@herasys.com
Date: 2027-06-16T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final draft: 12m renewal + $75k bridging credit (DocuSign)

Asha — attaching the redline-ready amendment and the DocuSign envelope link (internal link included). Summary of final points we implemented per your requests:
- 12-month term effective 2027-07-01 with baseline commit = 1,000,000 tokens/month.
- 20% price hold on baseline volume for the term.
- $75,000 bridging credit applied as a billing credit to Q3 invoices (line-item credit; will reduce invoice net due).
- 90-day pilot rate guarantee includes a 10% burst allowance over baseline; overage beyond 1.1x baseline billed at the standard overage rate.
- SLA stub included (median latency target + escalation contact) — legal will expand in full contract if you need a higher SLA.

Next steps:
1) Review the amendment and redline in DocuSign by 2027-06-25. (DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/HR-2027-014-sign)
2) Procurement approves and returns final PO; Redwood will apply the credit to first Q3 invoice after effective date.
3) Kickoff ops/hands-on onboarding for the pilot week of 2027-07-05.

If procurement needs a short meeting to finalize language, I'm available 6/17 or 6/18 afternoon. Thanks everyone — excited to support the Hera launch.

Best,
Logan
Logan Wright | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
